I’ve fixed a dyadic center average with a unit physical window and positive Gaussian smoothing at each fixed height. The arithmetic theorem supplies a difference-only projection; the full pair function also retains the pair’s common position and both transverse marks. I’m making that gap precise and working out the costs of the joint log-field route.

The log-field route has a useful constraint: a reference field that is harmonic across the observation window contributes exactly zero after the Laplacian extracts the zero density. A leading prime-only log model therefore cannot supply this pair function by itself. I’m reducing the remaining nonharmonic contribution to explicit mixed source moments, with the logarithmic singularities and center boundaries accounted for.

B06 is complete at its stated boundary: the notes now specify the joint moments needed and an explicit error budget for both the connected and full pair functions. Those moments have not been evaluated, so no canonical profile is claimed. I’m checking the saved handoff and preserving the earlier assessment files.

The key finding is that a harmonic log-field reference contributes zero when extracting the planar zero density. Can you explain the current state of the research at a high level, but including relevant equations?
I’ll check the latest notes and progress register, then explain the main objects, what has been established, and what remains open.

The main distinction is between defining the correlation function, controlling approximation errors, and actually computing the canonical function. The first two have written results; B07 specifies a certified route to the third. I’ll show how those stages connect through the equations.

The localized-correlation branch now has **a precise correlation framework, explicit approximation bounds, and a concrete plan for a certified finite computation**. The actual canonical pair function has not yet been computed, and no limiting correlation law has been established.

The central question is how zeros occur together near a moving observation center, retaining their imaginary coordinates and multiplicities. At time zero, the canonical function satisfies
\[
H_0(z)=\frac18\,\xi\!\left(\frac12-\frac{iz}{2}\right).
\]
A zeta zero \(\beta+i\gamma\) corresponds, using conjugation, to
\[
z=2\gamma+i(2\beta-1).
\]
Thus the real coordinate records height, while the imaginary coordinate records departure from the critical line. The framework accommodates both real and nonreal zeros without assuming RH.

Using the current pilot’s coordinates, let \(W_X(z)\) be a compact window around center \(X\), and define
\[
G_\epsilon(u)=\frac{e^{-|u|^2/(2\epsilon^2)}}{2\pi\epsilon^2},
\qquad
q_{j,X}(u)=W_X(z_j)\,G_\epsilon(X+u-z_j).
\]
Each zero contributes a Gaussian bump. The first intensity and the **factorial pair intensity** are
\[
r_X(u)=\sum_j q_{j,X}(u),
\qquad
R_{2,X}(u,v)=\sum_{j\ne k}q_{j,X}(u)q_{k,X}(v).
\]
The second expression counts ordered pairs of distinct labels. A zero of multiplicity \(m\) therefore contributes \(m(m-1)\) coincident pairs. Higher correlations follow the same construction with more distinct labels.

The randomness comes from choosing the center \(X\) uniformly on \([T,2T]\). The zero configuration itself is deterministic. Averaging gives the full pair function, while subtracting the product of mean intensities gives its connected part:
\[
\overline R_2(u,v)=\mathbb E_X R_{2,X}(u,v),
\qquad
C_T(u,v)=\overline R_2(u,v)
-\mathbb E_Xr_X(u)\,\mathbb E_Xr_X(v).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
C_T(u,v)
=\operatorname{Cov}_X(r_X(u),r_X(v))
-\mathbb E_X d_X(u,v),
\qquad
d_X(u,v)=\sum_jq_{j,X}(u)q_{j,X}(v).
\]
The last term removes pairing a label with itself. Because each \(q\) contains \(W_X\), this correction contains **\(W_X^2\)**. Both factors in a genuine pair use the same center \(X\).

The earlier analytical work established how to obtain these observables from the canonical function. Its basic bridge is the distributional identity
\[
\nu_0:=\sum_j\delta_{z_j}
=\frac{1}{2\pi}\Delta\log|H_0|.
\]
This converts suitably weighted zero statistics into integrals of the logarithm of the field. Under the stated disk and window hypotheses, the research provides explicit estimates of the schematic form
\[
\|F-\widehat F\|_\infty\le\delta
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\|\overline R_2-\overline{\widehat R}_2\|_\infty
\le K_T\delta^{\alpha_T},
\qquad \alpha_T>0,
\]
where \(F\) is a normalized canonical field. The constants depend on height and smoothing; both arithmetic and radial truncation tails must be included.

**That controls approximation error, but does not supply the correlation’s value.** B06 made the remaining analytical input precise: actual joint source moments at a common center, with certified errors. One-point estimates do not supply them. It also showed why a harmonic approximation to the logarithmic field cannot supply the planar zero density: its Laplacian vanishes on the relevant supports. The finite moment construction is valid, but its required polynomial degree may be enormous. These statements were accepted within their stated scope in the internal E08 assessment. [B06 analysis](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/08_theta_observables_newman_dynamics/03_operator_imaginary_time_evolution/02_localized_zero_correlations/notes/11_TND_OC_B06_CENTER_LAW_AND_JOINT_SOURCE_DECISION_20261108.md)

B07 therefore selected a direct finite route: **certify the complete zero inventory, then integrate its Gaussian pair contributions**. Completeness is essential. A list of proposed real zeros is accepted only if certified brackets account exactly for an independently certified count of all complex zeros in the region.

For the fixed pilot
\[
T=1000,\qquad X\sim\mathrm{Unif}[1000,2000],
\qquad \epsilon=\tfrac14,
\]
B07 derives continuous approximations \(Q_2,Q_C\) satisfying
\[
\max\!\left\{
\|\overline R_2-Q_2\|_\infty,\,
\|C_T-Q_C\|_\infty
\right\}
\le \frac{5249}{2^{24}}<\frac1{3000}
\]
on \(Q\times Q\), where \(Q=[-1,1]+i[-1,1]\). This is conditional on the specified gates: at most \(512\) certified labels, location error at most \(2^{-38}\), at most \(4096\) overlapping ordered pairs, and 20-node quadrature on each window piece. Arithmetic rounding is charged separately. These are proved design bounds, not measured canonical results. B07 currently has proof-author checking only. [B07 proof and contract](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/08_theta_observables_newman_dynamics/03_operator_imaginary_time_evolution/02_localized_zero_correlations/notes/13_TND_OC_B07_COMPLETE_DIVISOR_AND_GAUSSIAN_EVALUATOR_20261108.md)

**Next: [E] TND-OC-E09 — Sol.** Check those proof obligations and execute the bounded pilot. Success would give this branch a certified finite pair function and connected function, providing a concrete benchmark for later analytical work. Large-height asymptotics, quantitative higher correlations and Newman-time evolution remain further research questions.
